body.estimand_functional: \(P_x(Y=y)=T_{D,y}(p)=A_{D,y}(p)/B_{D,y}(p)\) for every \(D\in\mathfrak D\) on the equality branch

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed strictly positive multinomial law \(P\) after one certified input and its equality-branch circuit have been fixed.
sampling_model.units: The observations \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) are independent draws in the finite cell space \(\Omega\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention \(do(X=x)\) is a causal query, not a randomized sampling arm.
sampling_model.overlap: Membership \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) gives positive cells and positive recorded marginal denominators at the fixed law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no nonparametric nuisances; \(\widehat\tau_n=\tau(\widehat p_n)\) and \(\widehat V_n=J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)\{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p_n)-\widehat p_n\widehat p_n^{\mathsf T}\}J_{\tau}(\widehat p_n)^{\mathsf T}\) are computed from the fixed certified circuit.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 gives a sufficient graphical condition for simultaneous identification over a finite SA-MPDAG family.
Theorem 3.6 gives a necessary-and-sufficient criterion and generalized truncated factorization for one MPDAG.
Theorem 8 identifies a DAG factorization component by saturation of local and global Markov ideals.
Theorem 3 minimally enumerates distinct intervention functionals represented by one MPDAG.
IDP is sound and complete for causal-effect identification from one PAG.
A discrete causal query under one specified model compiles to a sharp polynomial program with anytime-valid outer bounds.
Resampling CI statistics and unioning graphwise intervals yields asymptotically correct coverage for a fixed effect after PC discovery.
SP consistently recovers the true MEC under the sparsest Markov representation condition.

body.tldr: Observational discovery can return several non-Markov-equivalent graphs with the same minimum edge count, and selecting one can change \(P_x(Y)\). SparseSIM-ID checks a nonempty certified tied family and a positive rational realization of the exact CI oracle, compiles every represented DAG's truncated factorization into a rational observed-table circuit, and then decides effect agreement on the strictly positive exact-oracle chamber. Fixed-order real-radical zero tests are a fast sufficient branch; otherwise exact real-closed-field feasibility returns either the common circuit with finite infeasibility certificates or an exact real-algebraic ambiguity table with isolating data. The certified four-binary-variable instance remains a rational strictness witness beyond the sufficient test of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo, and pointwise multinomial delta-method inference applies to a fixed certified equality-branch circuit.

project_justification.gap: Existing simultaneous-identification theory gives sufficient graphical conditions but not a necessary decision of common effects on the strictly positive exact-oracle law model. Saturated CI ideals alone do not select that sign chamber.
project_justification.niche: Minimum-edge ties are a structured and operationally important family in which graph-local Markov constraints are redundant. Common-effect identification therefore reduces to finitely many graph-indexed rational-function equalities tested on one explicit semialgebraic exact-oracle chamber.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a complete exact semialgebraic decision algorithm: each intervention signature is either infeasible off zero on the positive exact-oracle chamber, with a finite quantifier-elimination or Positivstellensatz certificate, or has an exact real-algebraic positive separator. It retains real-radical normal forms as a fast sufficient test, proves strictness over the closest graphical criterion with a concrete rational four-node witness, and attaches fixed-input plug-in inference to the common circuit.

body.related_work: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (Proceedings of the 42nd ICML, 2025, Theorem 3.2 and Section 4.2) give the closest causal boundary: their SA-MPDAG criterion is sufficient, and their necessity discussion requires a common law with unequal graphwise effects, but supplies no general rational-density or positive-chamber construction. Theorem 2 decides every certified tied-sparsest query, while Corollary 1 retains a positive rational instance on which their graphical test is undecided. Perkovic (2020, Theorem 3.6) supplies the graph-specific bucket truncated factorization adapted here into rational observed-cell circuits. Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005, Theorem 8) inform saturation by marginal factors, but saturation does not select the strictly positive exact-oracle chamber or impose the bit-zero inequalities. Tarski's real-closed-field decision method and Stengle's Positivstellensatz supply the generic exact feasibility and infeasibility machinery used after the graph-native compilation. Kahle, Rauh, and Sullivant (2017, Sections 3.1 and 3.3) explain why irrelevant CI components make positivity separate from ideal membership. Raskutti and Uhler (2018) define the tied minimum-edge discovery target without an effect-aware output policy. Guo and Perkovic (2021, Theorem 3), Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019, Section 4.2), and Duarte et al. (2024) respectively inform within-MPDAG effect quotienting, success-or-obstruction completeness, and certified polynomial compilation. Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024) motivate the distinction between discovery and estimation uncertainty; the plug-in theorem remains pointwise for one fixed certified population input.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The complete decision is finite but carries no useful uniform complexity or algebraic-height bound. Saturation by cells and denominators excludes components contained in their zero sets, but it neither imposes \(p_z>0\) nor the nonvanishing blocks for zero CI bits; consequently \(F_{D,y}\notin K_{\mathcal I}\) is only a trigger for semialgebraic testing and never an ambiguity certificate. A feasible general witness is guaranteed to be exactly real algebraic, not rational. Rational output with a uniform height bound remains the separate rational-atlas open question.
body.honest_scope: The exact CI oracle, background orientations, query, complete tied minimum-edge family, and a positive rational exact-oracle feasibility witness are fixed certified population inputs; empty graph families and unrealizable exact oracles are outside the accepted domain. The main result is complete semialgebraic decidability with exact real-algebraic separator output, not a general rational-point theorem and not a polynomial-time guarantee. The existing rational-atlas open question records whether every separating chamber admits a bounded-height rational witness. The four-variable certified table remains an explicit rational separator with minimum cell \(1/40\), exactly four elementary CIs, \(50\) I-map DAGs, exactly two four-edge minima in distinct MECs, and intervention probabilities \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). When the candidate family is one MPDAG and the oracle model equals that graph's positive Markov model, the decision specializes to the known single-family setting. Plug-in inference fixes one certified equality-branch circuit and one interior law; it is not selection-aware inference for an estimated oracle or graph tie set.
